subject: Sociology
title: Class, Gender & Bodies — The Sociology of the Body
blurb: Week-5 opens the unit's first big topic — the body — the lecturer's way, from a history of the toilet: private sex-gendered lavatories as a modern Western invention (urbanization, sanitary reform, Shove's practice theory of materials/competences/meanings). Part 1 runs class through Marx (profits vs wages, surplus value, exploitation, alienation), Weber (life chances + status + power) and Bourdieu (habitus, field, the four capitals). Part 2 does embodiment via Foucault (the medical gaze, biopower, docile bodies), Bourdieu's body habitus ('the social world is in the body'), Goffman's dramaturgy and Young's 'throwing like a girl'. Part 3 redefines sex vs gender vs sexuality (the sex-gender system; Semenya, Hubbard, the fined Norwegian handball team) and the contemporary body — the neoliberal toned body, Hockey's trainers and material culture (commoditisation vs singularisation), ageing/ill and non-human robotic bodies — closing on intersectional lenses for the take-home 'read the image' exam. Theory-dense: 10 tables, 0 plates, per-section reasoning & recall, all three readings integrated, ~36-question quiz.

subject: Sociology
title: Researching Everyday Life — Ethnography & the Go-Along
blurb: Week-4 shifts from theory to method: how do you actually study the everyday? Wraps up Garfinkel's ethnomethodology (breaching experiments) and Goffman's dramaturgy (front/back stage, impression management), then reads the self-checkout as Weber's rationalisation. Covers research design (deductive vs inductive, macro vs micro, quantitative/qualitative/mixed) and the core qualitative tool — ethnography: thick description, the two components (participant observation + fieldnotes), emic vs etic, the 'positioned subject'; its history (Malinowski's Trobriands, the Chicago School); and four landmark studies (Goffman's total institution, Willis's 'lads', Wacquant's carnal boxing sociology, Venkatesh's gang). Closes on the week's reading — Kusenbach's go-along and the five things it reveals that a sit-down interview can't (perception, spatial practices, biographies, social architecture, social realms). Method-dense: 9 tables, per-section reasoning & recall, ~31-question quiz.

subject: Human Cell & Molecular Biology
title: DNA Replication
blurb: Week-5 molecular biology (Helen Rizos, Parts I–III). Eukaryotic DNA replication end to end: the antiparallel 5′→3′ helix and how that directionality forces everything downstream; DNA packaging into chromosomes (p/q arms, banding, the 9p21 address); the semi-conservative principle; then the four steps — unwinding (origins, the ORC→Cdc6→MCM2-7 helicase, RPA, topoisomerases), priming (primase's RNA primers + Pol α), elongation (leading vs lagging, Okazaki fragments), and termination (FEN1, RNase H, DNA ligase). Plus the three replicative polymerases α/δ/ε compared, 3′-exonuclease proofreading and the PCNA sliding clamp, a fidelity worked example (~64,000 → ~6 errors per genome), and once-per-cycle licensing. 10 plates + reasoning/clinical boxes and a 30-question quiz.

subject: Musculoskeletal System
title: Upper Limb Nerve Supply
blurb: Week-5 upper-limb innervation (Dr Strkalj) — the natural pair to the blood-supply guide. One network, the brachial plexus (C5–T1), re-plaited level by level (roots → trunks → divisions → cords → branches) into five terminal nerves — musculocutaneous, median, ulnar, axillary, radial — each with its course, motor job, cutaneous patch and signature injury. Covers root/trunk side-branches (long thoracic → winged scapula, suprascapular), the carpal tunnel and Guyon's canal, dermatomes vs cutaneous-nerve maps, intrinsic-hand supply (all ulnar except LOAF) and bedside testing, plus full Clinical boxes on the classic lesions: Erb's (waiter's tip), Klumpke's (claw hand), carpal tunnel syndrome, wrist drop, and the axillary-nerve/dislocated-shoulder. 32 real plates + reasoning/clinical boxes and a quiz.

subject: Pharmacology Fundamentals
title: Drug Targets — Enzymes, Receptors & Transporters
blurb: L9 + L10 merged — the four protein target classes (receptors, ion channels, enzymes, transporters) and the three things a drug does to each. Enzymes as targets (reversible vs irreversible anticholinesterases, false substrates, the methotrexate/fluorouracil antifolates); the four receptor superfamilies decoded by location, effector, coupling, structure and timescale (ionotropic → GPCR → kinase-linked → nuclear, ms → hours), with the G-protein cycle, Gs/Gi/Gq, β-arrestin desensitisation, subtypes, allosteric modulation and biased agonism; and transporters as targets (passive vs active, SLC vs ABC/P-glycoprotein, SSRI/SNRI/TCA reuptake block). 21 real plates with reasoning + clinical angle on each.

subject: Cardiovascular, Renal & Respiratory Systems
title: Anatomy of the Heart & Blood Vessels
blurb: Where MHHS2402 turns from the airways to the pump. A complete decode of the Week 5 cardiovascular-anatomy lecture (LO1–LO10, all 70 slides): thoracic inlet and mediastinum; pericardium, heart surfaces and borders; the four chambers and their wall features; the AV and semilunar valves and the fibrous skeleton; the coronary tree and cardiac veins; the conduction system, cardiac nerves and referred pain; artery/vein/capillary wall structure; systemic vs pulmonary circulation; foetal circulation and its adult remnants; the aorta, carotids, azygos and portal systems; and surface anatomy with the four valve auscultation points. 28 real cadaveric/diagrammatic plates, each with the reasoning + clinical angle behind it.

subject: Musculoskeletal System
title: Upper Limb Blood Supply & Lymphatics
blurb: Week-5 upper-limb vasculature (Dr Strkalj). One arterial highway renamed at each landmark — subclavian → axillary (3 parts split by pec minor) → brachial (main arm supply, ends in the cubital fossa) → radial & ulnar → superficial & deep palmar arches — with anastomoses (scapula, elbow, hand) for collateral flow; the axilla and its walls; venous return via superficial veins (cephalic, basilic, median cubital) and deep venae comitantes; and lymphatic drainage through the five axillary node groups (pectoral, subscapular, humeral, central, apical). 5 real plates + reasoning/clinical boxes (pulses, Allen's test, venepuncture, breast-cancer staging) and a quiz.

subject: Musculoskeletal System
title: Muscle Physiology III — Reflexes
blurb: Week-5 reflexes (Dr Ban). What a reflex is (rapid, involuntary, spinal; overridable unless a cord lesion sits above the arc), the 5-part reflex arc, the two muscle proprioceptors (spindle → stretch/length → contract vs Golgi tendon organ → tension/force → relax), monosynaptic vs polysynaptic circuits, ipsilateral reciprocal inhibition, the contralateral crossed-extensor reflex (postural stability), and rhythmic movement via central pattern generators. 4 real plates + reasoning/clinical boxes and a quiz.

subject: Sociology
title: Not So Mundane — Theorising the Everyday
blurb: Week-3 theory toolkit — the thinkers who make the everyday strange. Why theorise the mundane (Highmore, Durkheim's moral consensus, reflexivity); Sztompka's 5-point framework for analysing a social event; the footpath as politics (Blomley's pedestrianism, Jim Crow, Peckham); then the roster: Weber (rationalisation, bureaucracy's 5 features, the iron cage), Hochschild (emotional labour — display vs feeling rules, surface vs deep acting), Simmel (forms, the stranger, the blasé metropolis, philosophy of money), Lefebvre (the production of space + spatial triad) & Foucault (panopticon, internalised power), Garfinkel (ethnomethodology & breaching experiments) + symbolic interactionism, and Goffman (dramaturgy, front/back stage) applied to Scott's swimming-pool study. Theory-dense: 7 tables + per-section reasoning & recall, ~50-question quiz.

subject: Sociology
title: The Meaning of Everyday Life
blurb: Week-2 sociology of everyday life. The seven characteristics of the everyday (repetition/Durkheim, habit & habitus/Mauss & Bourdieu, home & ontological security/Giddens, normality, the democratic 'even the Queen', the political, and its history), two everyday sites read closely (the politics of waiting at the bus stop; the sociology of the queue + the Saarbrücken experiment), then the everyday situated in MODERNITY via the Inglis reading — Weber's rationalization/bureaucracy/iron cage, Hochschild's feeling rules, Simmel's money mentality & blasé attitude, revolt into style, invented traditions, tourism and the ironic post-tourist. 2 plates, per-section reasoning + recall, ~45-question quiz.

subject: Sociology
title: What is Everyday Life? — Thinking Sociologically
blurb: Week-1 intro to sociology through the everyday. The sociological imagination (C. Wright Mills), the monobloc chair as 'making something out of nothing' (Zuckerman's context-free object), what 'the everyday' is, structure vs agency, a full unpacking of tooth-brushing (embodied practice → class & public health → medicalisation → the 'illusion of choice' under global capitalism), and the comedy reading (Seinfeld: the significance of the insignificant). 4 real plates from the lecture, per-section reasoning + recall, and a 60+ question quiz.

subject: Human Cell & Molecular Biology
title: Meiosis — Cell Division & Genetic Variation
blurb: Week-4 meiosis (sequel to W3 mitosis) — why meiosis exists (haploid gametes so fertilisation restores 2n), meiosis vs mitosis, the two divisions (meiosis I separates homologues, meiosis II separates sister chromatids), the three sources of genetic variation (crossing over in prophase I + chiasmata, independent assortment at metaphase I, random assortment at metaphase II) and non-disjunction/aneuploidy (Down 47+21, Turner 45,X, Klinefelter 47,XXY). 7 plates with the reasoning + clinical angle behind each.

subject: Human Cell & Molecular Biology
title: Cell Division — DNA Organisation & Mitosis
blurb: Week-3 cell division, both modules merged — packaging the genome (nucleus vs nucleoid, the DNA→nucleosome→chromatin→chromosome ladder), euchromatin vs heterochromatin & epigenetic control, chromosome structure (sister chromatids, centromere, p/q arms, centromere classification), telomeres/senescence/telomerase, the human karyotype (46/23, autosomes/sex) & locus nomenclature, then why cells divide (mitosis vs meiosis, binary fission) and the mitotic cell cycle (interphase, PMAT, checkpoints). 8 plates; §5 mitosis follows the module's learning objectives (delivered as video).

subject: Musculoskeletal System
title: Anatomy of the Hand
blurb: L5 — the hand built from the ground up: the 27 bones and the carpal tunnel (9 tendons + median nerve), the joints classified by movement (condyloid wrist, saddle thumb CMC, hinge IP) with rheumatoid arthritis, the extrinsic and intrinsic muscles and their ulnar/median nerve supply (MEat LOAF, DAB/PAD), and the fascia (palmar aponeurosis, retinacula, extensor hoods) with carpal tunnel syndrome, mallet finger and tenosynovitis. 12 plates with the reasoning + clinical angle behind each.

subject: Pharmacology Fundamentals
title: Pharmacodynamics — Drug Action & Quantification
blurb: L7 + L8 merged — the four drug targets (receptors, ion channels, enzymes, transporters), the language of binding (specificity, selectivity, affinity/KD), and quantifying drug effect with concentration–response curves: full/partial/inverse agonists, competitive vs irreversible antagonists, receptor reserve, allosteric modulation (benzodiazepines), and efficacy vs potency (Emax, EC50). 9 plates with the reasoning + clinical angle behind each.

subject: Musculoskeletal System
title: Muscle Physiology II — Muscle Tension & Performance
blurb: The sequel to Muscle Physiology I — the three energy systems (phosphagen/PCr, anaerobic glycolysis, aerobic) and fatigue/recovery; what sets muscle tension (the length–tension curve, the structural proteins nebulin/titin/dystrophin, and Duchenne muscular dystrophy); stimulation (motor units, treppe/summation/tetanus, muscle tone, MND) and contraction types; and the three fibre types tuned by genetics and training. 12 plates with the reasoning + clinical angle behind each.

subject: Cardiovascular, Renal & Respiratory Systems
title: Respiratory Regulation Inputs
blurb: The control of breathing — the homeostatic feedback loop, the three regulated arterial parameters (O2, CO2, pH), the central & peripheral chemoreceptors, the reflex inputs (Hering-Breuer, J-receptors, irritant/proprioceptor/metaboreceptor/thermoreceptor/pain, cough/sneeze/swallow) and the brainstem respiratory centre (DRG/VRG/pons, transection experiments), tied together by the change→detect→process→output→action exam chain. 8 plates with the reasoning + clinical angle behind each.

subject: Human Cell & Molecular Biology
title: Cell Structure & Interactions
blurb: The whole four-part series decoded — the cytoskeleton (actin, microtubules, intermediate filaments, motor proteins, division, migration, cilia), the extracellular matrix (GAGs & proteoglycans, collagen, elastin, fibronectin, basal lamina), and the cell junctions that wire cell to cell and cell to matrix — each with its reasoning and clinical angle.

subject: Pharmacology Fundamentals
title: Introduction to Pharmacology
blurb: Week-1 foundations — what counts as a drug, the branches of pharmacology, and the core pharmacokinetics-vs-pharmacodynamics distinction, plus the tutorial's drug classes.

subject: Musculoskeletal System
title: Musculoskeletal System — Introduction
blurb: The full introduction module — bone tissue, ossification, bone & joint classification, muscle, the upper limb and limb development — decoded with the module's own figures and the reasoning + clinical angle behind each fact.

subject: Musculoskeletal System
title: Arm, Elbow & Anterior Forearm
blurb: L3 built the way the limb is built — distal humerus & proximal radius/ulna, the elbow & radioulnar joints, the arm muscles, and the anterior forearm flexors — with the reasoning, leverage and clinical angle behind each.

subject: Human Cell & Molecular Biology
title: Cell Organisation
blurb: The cell from the outside in — what every cell shares, how prokaryotes and eukaryotes differ, and each organelle decoded. Built from your module, using its own figures.

subject: Cardiovascular, Renal & Respiratory Systems
title: Anatomy of the Respiratory System — Pt 1
blurb: The head-and-neck scaffolding for breathing — the bones the airway is carved from, and the nerves that thread through them. Built from your lecture, with every slide decoded.

subject: Musculoskeletal System
title: Bone Physiology I
blurb: Bone as a living, self-rebuilding organ — the four cells, structure→strength, formation & growth, lifelong remodelling, hormonal control (PTH/vitamin D/calcitonin, RANKL/OPG), and the metabolic & genetic disorders when the balance tips.

subject: Pharmacology Fundamentals
title: Pharmacokinetics — Absorption & Distribution
blurb: Three lectures merged (Welcome + L3 + L4) — the ADME framework, how drugs cross membranes, absorption (pKa & ion trapping, routes), bioavailability & first-pass (with a worked dose example), and distribution (compartments, protein binding, volume of distribution).

subject: Cardiovascular, Renal & Respiratory Systems
title: Respiratory Anatomy — Pt 2
blurb: Part 2 — down the neck (triangles, fascia, muscles), through the larynx (cartilages, vocal cords, divisions, nerves), the thoracic wall, diaphragm & breathing mechanics, then the pleura, bronchial tree, lungs and gas exchange.

subject: Musculoskeletal System
title: Posterior Forearm & Wrist
blurb: L4 — the posterior (extensor) compartment as the hand's 'remote control', the bones of the hand, the wrist joint, then bone fractures and the four-stage healing cascade. 20 plates with the reasoning + clinical angle behind each.

subject: Pharmacology Fundamentals
title: Drug Elimination — Metabolism, Excretion & PK
blurb: L5 + L6 merged — hepatic metabolism (Phase 1/2, CYP450, prodrugs), renal & hepatobiliary excretion, and the PK parameters (bioavailability, Vd, clearance, half-life, steady state) with first- vs zero-order kinetics and worked examples.

subject: Musculoskeletal System
title: Shoulder Region
blurb: L2 built the way the shoulder is built - the bones (clavicle, scapula, proximal humerus), the three joints (sternoclavicular, acromioclavicular, glenohumeral) and their stability, then every extrinsic and intrinsic muscle and the rotator cuff (SITS) - each fact noted and explained with its reasoning and clinical angle.

subject: Musculoskeletal System
title: Bone Physiology II — Fracture & Healing
blurb: The dedicated deep-dive on fracture healing — the haematoma cascade (hypoxia to VEGF to angiogenesis), soft then bony callus, remodelling, and the malunion/nonunion failures — building on Bone Physiology I.

subject: Musculoskeletal System
title: Muscle Physiology I — Excitation & Contraction
blurb: From molecule to movement — skeletal-muscle structure (sarcomere, T-tubules, SR), the neuromuscular junction (with drug, neurotoxin and myasthenia-gravis angles), and the sliding-filament mechanism of contraction, relaxation and rigor mortis. 14 plates.

subject: Cardiovascular, Renal & Respiratory Systems
title: Ventilation & Gas Exchange
blurb: The physics of breathing — the five respiratory functions (incl. surfactant/Laplace), the fluid-movement laws (Boyle, Poiseuille), lung mechanics, volumes & capacities, gas diffusion (Fick, Dalton, the oxygen cascade) and the ventilation-perfusion ratio, with worked examples.
